sourcedFrom: THUNDER CHICKEN BY Q™ / TRASH PANDA BY Q™ / CHERRY BOMB™ FAST-ATTACH MUZZLE BRAKE BY Q™ — NOT PRINTED — this sheet carries no revision number (unlike the ERECTOR and NELSON sheets, which print REV 1.0) (2021)
cleanIntro: A 6.9 inch titanium 7.62 can, 11.8 oz, that lives on Q's Quickie fast-attach interface — it does not thread to a barrel, it threads to a Cherry Bomb muzzle brake that stays on the host. Q publishes no disassembly for it: the whole of its teardown is taking it off the brake. Everything below comes off the one tech-data sheet Q publishes for the Thunder Chicken and Trash Panda together, so read the figures for YOUR can and not its longer brother.

steps.title: Clear the host before the Trash Panda is touched
steps.action: Magazine out, action open, then look into the chamber and magazine well AND put a finger in. Q asks for both a physical and a visual inspection before any silencer comes off its host. On a 300 BLK or 7.62 host the chamber is deep and shadowed and the eye alone is not enough.
steps.prose: Do this before the can, not after. Breaking a suppressor off a brake is a two-handed job, and both hands are away from the trigger only if the gun is already clear.
steps.quote: BEFORE REMOVING ANY SILENCER FROM ITS HOST, REMOVE THE MAGAZINE FROM YOUR FIREARM, MAKE SURE THE ACTION IS OPEN AND THE FIREARM IS UNLOADED BY PERFORMING A PHYSICAL AND VISUAL INSPECTION OF THE CHAMBER AND MAGAZINE WELL.
steps.cite: THUNDER CHICKEN BY Q™ / TRASH PANDA BY Q™ / CHERRY BOMB™ FAST-ATTACH MUZZLE BRAKE BY Q™ — NOT PRINTED — this sheet carries no revision number (unlike the ERECTOR and NELSON sheets, which print REV 1.0) — REMOVAL, p.1
steps.warn: The firearm is not clear until the chamber has been both seen and felt.

steps.title: The host firearm's own manual is the clearing authority
steps.action: This sheet tells you when to clear the gun; it never tells you how, because it does not know what the can is bolted to. Use the operating manual for your own rifle for the clearing sequence and use this sheet only for the suppressor. Q also states outright that this sheet is not the whole document — a separate FINE PRINT sheet ships with the can and must be read alongside it.
steps.prose: A one-page tech-data sheet is a deliberately thin document. Treating it as complete is the mistake it invites.
steps.caution: Two documents ship with this can. This is one of them.
steps.quote: BEFORE USING THIS SILENCER: BE CERTAIN YOU HAVE READ AND UNDERSTAND THIS MANUAL AND THE ACCOMPANYING “FINE PRINT” SHEET.
steps.cite: THUNDER CHICKEN BY Q™ / TRASH PANDA BY Q™ / CHERRY BOMB™ FAST-ATTACH MUZZLE BRAKE BY Q™ — NOT PRINTED — this sheet carries no revision number (unlike the ERECTOR and NELSON sheets, which print REV 1.0) — MORE LAWYER SHIT, p.1

steps.title: Trash Panda ceiling — 7.62mm or smaller projectiles
steps.action: Confirm the host's bore before mounting. Q rates the Thunder Chicken and the Trash Panda for 7.62mm or smaller projectiles, and the SPECS block carrying the Trash Panda's name lists 7.62 NATO, 300 BLK and 300 WM. That is a projectile-diameter limit rather than a chambering list, so a larger bore is outside the design no matter what the pressure is.
steps.prose: The two cans on this sheet share the rating and differ in everything else: 6.9 in and 11.8 oz for the Trash Panda against 8.1 in and 14.7 oz for the Thunder Chicken. Read the block with your can's name on it.
steps.quote: THE THUNDER CHICKEN & TRASH PANDA SILENCERS ARE FOR USE WITH 7.62MM OR SMALLER PROJECTILES.
steps.cite: THUNDER CHICKEN BY Q™ / TRASH PANDA BY Q™ / CHERRY BOMB™ FAST-ATTACH MUZZLE BRAKE BY Q™ — NOT PRINTED — this sheet carries no revision number (unlike the ERECTOR and NELSON sheets, which print REV 1.0) — MORE LAWYER SHIT, p.1
steps.warn: 7.62mm is the ceiling for this can.

steps.title: Factory SAAMI or C.I.P. ammunition only
steps.action: Check what is in the magazine before the can goes on. Q restricts this silencer to factory certified SAAMI or C.I.P. ammunition, so handloads and remanufactured rounds sit outside the specification and are the ammunition end of Q's own baffle-strike list.
steps.prose: On a fast-attach can the alignment is set by the brake rather than by the barrel threads, so an out-of-spec round that starts to keyhole has nothing to correct it before it reaches the first baffle.
steps.quote: ONLY USE FACTORY CERTIFIED SAAMI/C.I.P. AMMUNITION WITH THIS SILENCER by Q.
steps.cite: THUNDER CHICKEN BY Q™ / TRASH PANDA BY Q™ / CHERRY BOMB™ FAST-ATTACH MUZZLE BRAKE BY Q™ — NOT PRINTED — this sheet carries no revision number (unlike the ERECTOR and NELSON sheets, which print REV 1.0) — MORE LAWYER SHIT, p.1

steps.title: Let it cool before you put a hand on it
steps.action: If you have just finished shooting, leave it a minute before touching anything. Q's wording is blunt about it. Titanium sheds heat slowly and 7.62 puts a lot into a 6.9 inch tube, so a bare hand on the body straight off a string is a burn rather than a warning.
steps.prose: The temptation is to grab the can because the wrench flats are right there. The flats are on the hottest part of it. Q's own sentence opens "IF YOU JUST FINISHED SHOOTING, I'D WAIT A MINUTE" before this, separated by an ellipsis the manual itself prints. The citation is cut to the contiguous half so that nothing is elided by us.
steps.cite: THUNDER CHICKEN BY Q™ / TRASH PANDA BY Q™ / CHERRY BOMB™ FAST-ATTACH MUZZLE BRAKE BY Q™ — NOT PRINTED — this sheet carries no revision number (unlike the ERECTOR and NELSON sheets, which print REV 1.0) — REMOVAL, p.1
steps.warn: Hot titanium looks exactly like cold titanium.

steps.title: Take the Trash Panda off the Cherry Bomb
steps.action: Put a wrench on the 1 inch SAE flats at the rear of the can — Q machines them there for exactly this, with a second 3/4 inch set at the front for cans that live under a handguard — and turn counter-clockwise. That is the whole removal: the can unthreads off the brake and comes away in your hand.
steps.prose: Q's own removal step reads "Le y loosey. You're done." — the ft ligature is dropped by the text extraction. There is nothing after it, because there is nothing else on this can that comes apart.
steps.caution: Use the rear flats. Gripping the tube body to break the joint is how a thin titanium tube gets crushed.
steps.quote: 1.Righty tighty. The Thunder Chicken and Trash Panda silencers feature 1 inch SAE ﬂats on the rear. We recommend you use these for install and removal. They also feature 3/4 SAE ﬂats on the front for silencers installed under a handguard.
steps.cite: THUNDER CHICKEN BY Q™ / TRASH PANDA BY Q™ / CHERRY BOMB™ FAST-ATTACH MUZZLE BRAKE BY Q™ — NOT PRINTED — this sheet carries no revision number (unlike the ERECTOR and NELSON sheets, which print REV 1.0) — SILENCER INSTALLATION, p.1

steps.title: The Cherry Bomb stays on the barrel
steps.action: Do not chase the brake off with the can. The Cherry Bomb is torqued to 20-30 lbs onto the host barrel with Rocksett on the threads, and it is the datum the Trash Panda indexes off — every time that joint is broken the alignment the can depends on is disturbed. Leave it fitted.
steps.prose: It also carries a thread-pitch decision: a 5/8-24 barrel takes the 5/8-24 Cherry Bomb and a 1/2-28 barrel takes the 1/2-28 one, and that is not something the can can absorb if it is got wrong.
steps.quote: 5.Using a 1/2 inch socket, tighten the Cherry Bomb clockwise onto your host ﬁrearm to 20-30 lbs.
steps.cite: THUNDER CHICKEN BY Q™ / TRASH PANDA BY Q™ / CHERRY BOMB™ FAST-ATTACH MUZZLE BRAKE BY Q™ — NOT PRINTED — this sheet carries no revision number (unlike the ERECTOR and NELSON sheets, which print REV 1.0) — ASSEMBLY — Cherry Bomb installation, p.1
steps.warn: DO NOT USE WASHERS, SHIMS, OR JAM NUTS WHEN INSTALLING THE CHERRY BOMB ONTO THE HOST BARREL.

steps.title: Clean the taper and the threads, not the inside
steps.action: With the can off, clean the Cherry Bomb's taper, its shoulder and its threads, and the matching features in the back of the Trash Panda. That interface is what holds the can concentric to the bore, and carbon on it is what walks a can off centre and puts a bullet into a baffle. Brass or nylon brush, or solvent-moistened Scotch-Brite — steel tools are barred.
steps.prose: This is the maintenance that actually matters on a fast-attach can. The inside will go a very long time; the mating surfaces will not.
steps.caution: DO NOT USE STEEL TOOLS FOR CLEANING.
steps.quote: 1.Clean the Cherry Bomb’s taper / shoulder and threads as well as the corresponding silencer features of any fouling. This will help with alignment of the silencer to the barrel’s axis, ensuring optimal performance.
steps.cite: THUNDER CHICKEN BY Q™ / TRASH PANDA BY Q™ / CHERRY BOMB™ FAST-ATTACH MUZZLE BRAKE BY Q™ — NOT PRINTED — this sheet carries no revision number (unlike the ERECTOR and NELSON sheets, which print REV 1.0) — CLEANING & MAINTENANCE, p.1

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The Trash Panda is off the Cherry Bomb and the brake is still on the barrel — that is the entire strip Q publishes for this can. There is no baffle stack to pull and no end cap to unscrew: the sheet has a REMOVAL section and no disassembly section at all. Where the inside genuinely needs attention, Q's answer is a bath and not a teardown.
steps.prose: A centrefire rifle can also needs far less of this than a rimfire or a pistol can, and Q says so plainly — the pressures and temperatures burn most of it out on their own.
steps.quote: • A CENTERFIRE RIFLE SILENCER DOES NOT REQUIRE THE SAME CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE AS A RIMFIRE OR PISTOL SILENCER DUE TO THE HIGHER PRESSURES AND TEMPERATURES OF THE CARTRIDGES.
steps.cite: THUNDER CHICKEN BY Q™ / TRASH PANDA BY Q™ / CHERRY BOMB™ FAST-ATTACH MUZZLE BRAKE BY Q™ — NOT PRINTED — this sheet carries no revision number (unlike the ERECTOR and NELSON sheets, which print REV 1.0) — CLEANING & MAINTENANCE, p.1

deepAbsentReason: Q PUBLISHES NO DISASSEMBLY FOR THE TRASH PANDA. Its tech-data sheet carries a REMOVAL section whose entire content is taking the can off the Cherry Bomb, and no disassembly section of any kind — unlike Q's own EL CAMINO and ERECTOR sheets, which print step-by-step teardowns. The only deep-cleaning instruction for this can is to submerge it assembled: 2.If you wish to clean this silencer, we recommend submerging it in a copper solvent or an ultrasonic cleaner. Inventing a baffle teardown for a can whose maker documents none would be fabrication, so no deep clean is offered.

cleaning.name: CHERRY BOMB INTERFACE
tasks: Clean the Cherry Bomb's taper, shoulder and threads of fouling
Clean the matching taper and threads inside the rear of the Trash Panda
Use solvent-moistened Scotch-Brite or a brass or nylon brush — never steel
Confirm the brake is still tight on the barrel at 20-30 lbs before refitting

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Wipe carbon off the 1 inch rear flats and the 3/4 inch front flats so a wrench still seats square
Check the tube for dents or bulges — a titanium tube shows a baffle strike from the outside
Wear eye protection: Q calls for PPE for all firearms cleaning and maintenance

cleaning.name: BORE (ASSEMBLED ONLY)
tasks: If the inside needs work, submerge the whole can in copper solvent or run it in an ultrasonic cleaner
Rinse it and make sure it is fully drained before firing
Never fire a can with solvent still standing in it

reassembly: Confirm the Cherry Bomb is still seated and tight on the host barrel; no washers, shims or jam nuts under it.
Start the Trash Panda onto the Cherry Bomb by hand and turn it clockwise — righty tighty.
Tighten clockwise onto the Cherry Bomb to 10-15 lbs using the 1 inch SAE flats on the rear.
Do not use thread lock at the silencer-to-brake joint; Q bars it on a Quickie fast-attach interface.
fncheck: With the Trash Panda tightened onto the Cherry Bomb, check that it sits straight to the bore with no visible cant and that it does not rock or rattle on the brake. Look down the tube from the muzzle end and confirm the exit is clear and unmarked. Any doubt about alignment, or any sign of a strike around the exit hole, and it does not get fired.
